title.narrative: Building Opportunities for Refugee and Host Community Resilience and Self-Reliance (Main and Flexible Mechanisms)

description.narrative: The Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei Settlement in Turkana County, and the Dadaab Refugee Complex in Garissa County collectively accommodate 84% of Kenya's refugees and asylum-seekers, a status maintained for many years. These regions, known for their low population density and economic hardship, face distinct challenges. Dadaab grapples with significant security concerns, demanding substantial resources for safety measures due to an unpredictable environment. Conversely, Kakuma demonstrates a harmonious coexistence between refugee and host communities. The Kalobeyei Integrated Socio-Economic Development Plan (KISEDP), governing operations with Phase I ending in 2022 and Phase II launched in March 2023, serves as a comprehensive framework. Aligned with international, regional, and local legal frameworks and plans, this multi-year, multi-sectoral initiative led by the government aims to bolster inclusive service delivery, fortify local capacities, enhance legal policies, promote investment and job creation, and bolster community resilience. Moreover, it seeks to empower individuals with skills for effective functioning within this context and to uplift the local economy. The response involves diverse stakeholders, including development entities, private sectors, financial institutions, academia, civil society, and others contributing to this integrated effort. Additionally, Garissa County has recently finalized the Garissa Integrated Socio-Economic Development Plan (GISEDP), integrated within the respective County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs).
